defects: Hypothesis differs from gold: gold requires `{x ∈ l₁ | p x}.Subsingleton`, i.e. at most one *distinct value* among the list's p-satisfying elements (duplicates of that value are fine), whereas produced requires `(l.filter p).length ≤ 1`, i.e. at most one *occurrence/position* in the list satisfies p. These are not equivalent: e.g. l = [a, a] with p a = true satisfies gold's hypothesis (the set {a} is a subsingleton) but violates produced's hypothesis (filter length = 2). Produced's hypothesis strictly implies gold's but not conversely, so the produced theorem is a strictly weaker/special case of the gold theorem, not the same proposition.
